meaning: The physical table this definition belongs to.
The database type the definition applies to, as the source names it.
The SQL statement when the table's table_type is 'select'; otherwise the name of the object in the database.

meaning: Row identifier: <table row_id>.<column name>.
The estate this row belongs to: the name of the estate folder that was extracted.
note: Named rpd_id for compatibility with the first Knowledge Base; it holds the estate name.

meaning: The physical table the column belongs to.
The column's name.
The data type as the source gives it, for example VARCHAR or DOUBLE.
The source's special-type marker for the column; usually 'none'.
The precision (length) as the source gives it; empty when not recorded.
Whether the column may be empty, as the source gives it: 'true', or empty when the source does not carry the attribute.
note: In both sample repositories the attribute is written only as 'true' (635 columns) and is absent on the rest (461 columns); 'false' never occurs. So the export appears to write it only when it is true, and an absent attribute most likely means the column is not nullable in the repository. The files do not state that, so the cell is left empty and nothing is filled in. The repository's setting is also not proof of the constraint in the database.

meaning: The column's external name in the source, when it has one.
The scale (the number of digits after the decimal point) as the source gives it; empty when not recorded.
note: Empty means the source says nothing; it does not mean 0. Not in the first attempt's Knowledge Base (deliberate difference 31).

meaning: The column's place among the table's columns in the repository, counting from 1; a whole number.
note: The order the repository lists the columns in. Sort a table's columns by this number to get that order: the rows of this table are in Row identifier order. It is not proof of the order in the database. Numbers can have gaps (a column left out for having no name still takes its place). Not in the first attempt's Knowledge Base (deliberate difference 31).

meaning: For a column of an alias table, the column of the aliased table it stands for; empty for any other column.
note: Also empty when the source gives an alias column no such link (the sampleapp repository has no alias; bi-analytics-2013 has the link on 101 columns), or the link did not resolve (no error row). Not in the first attempt's Knowledge Base (deliberate difference 37).

meaning: Row identifier: <table row_id>.<foreign key name> for a foreign key (.fk when it has no name); <estate>::phys::joins.<join name> for a complex join.
note: A foreign key and a column of the same table with the same name have the same identifier text; they are rows of different tables. 'joins' in a complex join's identifier is a fixed word, not a database or schema.

meaning: The estate this row belongs to: the name of the estate folder that was extracted.
note: Named rpd_id for compatibility with the first Knowledge Base; it holds the estate name.

meaning: 'foreign_key' or 'complex_join'.
note: Read kind first: it decides which of the other columns are filled.

meaning: The foreign key's or the join's name in the source.
For a foreign key, the table the key is declared on; for a complex join, the first of its two tables.
note: For a complex join, empty when the table was not found; no error row is written for that.

meaning: For a complex join, the second of its two tables; for a foreign key, the table it points at: the table that holds the key the foreign key refers to.
note: For a foreign key, empty when the source names no key or the key was not found (then errors.csv has an unresolved_reference row for the foreign key). The first attempt's Knowledge Base left it empty for every foreign key (deliberate difference 26).

meaning: For a complex join, the cardinality as the source writes it, for example 'ONE TO ONE'; empty for a foreign key.
note: Neither kind carries a join type (inner or outer); only logical joins do, in bmm_joins.

meaning: The template text of the join condition of a complex join (always empty for a foreign key), with %1, %2 ... where it names other objects; empty when there is none.
note: Kept exactly as the source wrote it; nothing is trimmed. Leading and trailing spaces are real. May start with '-' or '=' and may span several lines. %1, %2 ... stand for the entries of the matching _refs column, in order.

meaning: The same text of the join condition of a complex join (always empty for a foreign key) with the names filled in, as OBIEE shows it; empty when there is none.
note: Kept exactly as the source wrote it; nothing is trimmed. Written by OBIEE from the template; use it to read the formula, and the _refs column to follow it.

meaning: The objects that %1, %2 ... stand for in the join condition of a complex join (always empty for a foreign key), as Row identifiers.
note: One Row identifier per line, in placeholder order: line 1 is %1. Split on the line feed only; identifiers contain spaces. An empty line is a reference that did not resolve (errors.csv has an unresolved_reference row); a cell that is wholly empty is either no references or a single one that did not resolve. The entries point at different tables, so look an identifier up by its layer part and its shape.

meaning: For a foreign key, the key's own columns as Row identifiers of physical_columns, in source order; always empty for a complex join.
note: One Row identifier per line; split on the line feed only. An empty line is a column that was not found. These are the columns of the table in table1_id; the columns they point at are in referenced_columns.

meaning: For a foreign key, the columns of the key it points at, as Row identifiers of physical_columns: columns of the table in table2_id. Always empty for a complex join.
note: One Row identifier per line, in the source order of the referenced key; split on the line feed only. Line n pairs with line n of columns: the join is columns[n] = referenced_columns[n]. An empty line is a column that was not found; an empty cell on a foreign key row means the key it points at was not found. Not in the first attempt's Knowledge Base (deliberate difference 26).

meaning: Row identifier: <table row_id>.key.<key name> (.key.unnamed-<n> for the n-th key of the table when it has no name).
note: 'key' is a fixed word, so that a key and a column of the same name have different identifiers.

meaning: The estate this row belongs to: the name of the estate folder that was extracted.

meaning: The physical table the key is declared on.
The key's name in the repository.

meaning: The key's columns, as Row identifiers of physical_columns: columns of the table in table_id.
note: One Row identifier per line, in source order; split on the line feed only. An empty line is a column that was not found; a cell that is wholly empty is a key that lists no column, or one column that was not found. The repository has no flag that says whether a physical key is the table's primary key, so this table has no such column: a table with one key has one candidate, a table with several has several. A foreign key that points at this key has the same list in physical_joins.referenced_columns.

The fact's name: slicer_version, sliced_at, knowledge_base, kb_extracted_at, kb_extractor_version, rpd_ids, halves_present:<estate>, cut_by, subject_area, subject_area_id (a subject-area Slice), tab, subject_areas, subject_area_ids, decisions (a tab Slice), unparsed_identifiers_only, boundary_rows, errors_not_copied, unparsed_not_copied, unparsed_not_copied_by_type, not_in_slice:<what>, max_packet_lines, rows, units or tables.
The fact's value.
note: 'subject_area' is the subject area's name exactly as the repository has it; the folder name is a simplified form of it. 'tables': the table names separated by single spaces; read the table list from here, not from the folder. 'sliced_at' is the only time stamp in the Slice. 'boundary_rows': how many rows are in the Slice only so that a reference from another row resolves. 'errors_not_copied' and 'unparsed_not_copied': how many rows of the Knowledge Base's errors and unparsed tables are not about an object or object type in this Slice and were left out, by kind. 'unparsed_not_copied_by_type': the same rows of unparsed counted by kind and object type, one line each inside the value: kind, object type, number of rows, sum of their occurrences, separated by ' | '. 'max_packet_lines': the most lines a packet of this Slice may have (the slice command's --max-packet-lines). 'not_in_slice:<what>': how many rows of the Knowledge Base that belong to no subject area are not in this Slice (permissions_without_target, role_privileges, init_blocks, variables); the overview packet says where to find them. 'cut_by': subject_area or tab. 'tab': the tab's folder name; 'subject_areas' and 'subject_area_ids': the subject areas the tab's confirmed columns are in, one per line; 'decisions': counts of the tab's decisions and items. 'unparsed_identifiers_only': the details of the unparsed rows that are only an identifier of an element whose content is read, one per line; the gaps packet lists them apart.
